newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares lower after slide on Wall Street.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares lower after slide on Wall Street.

text.p: Israeli shares closed lower on Tuesday after Wall Street's 49-point slide overnight, traders said.
The benchmark Mishtanim index of top 100 shares fell 0.86 percent, or 2.24 points, to 257.31 on all-share turnover of 147 million shekels against 150 million shekels on Monday.
The Maof 25 blue chip index closed 0.97 percent lower at 265.79.
"The market was reacting to the Dow's decline. The underlying tone is still bullish and even today many shares rose," said Yoram Ben-Yaeir of Ahrayut Investment Management.

"The decline of Israeli shares traded in New York had a negative impact on trading today, but I do not think that this was the only reason for the decline," said Doron Tsur, head of research at Sahar Securities.

Tsur said it is good that the market is falling since, he said, it had risen too fast "with no firm base". With fourth-quarter company results due to come out soon, he said, the trend would become even more selective.
Ben-Yaeir said he expected the market to stabilise at its current level before resuming its climb.

Makhteshim Chemical Works surged 4.0 percent to 2,007 agorot. The company said on Tuesday it had signed a pact with Dow Chemical Co giving Makhteshim exclusive rights to distribute and produce vinyl esters in Israel and indicated the pact might lead to a wider relationship.

The most active shares were Bank Hapoalim, which rose 2.75 percent to 664 agorot on turnover of 13 million shekels; Clal Insurance, which surged 5.5 percent to 3,181 agorot on volume of 5 million shekels; and Formula Systems, which jumped 5.0 percent to 4,689 agorot on volume of 4.7 million shekels.
